description: A farm horse that outlived its farm. It still waits at the gate each dusk for a hand that never comes.
lore: The gate is still standing — two posts and a bar in open grass, the farm gone out from behind it. At dusk the horse comes up the slope, takes its place on the field side facing where the yard was, and waits about an hour to be brought in. The hand it waits for might be at a fire three days' walk from here, no longer able to tell you it ever owned a horse. It might never have woken at all.

[[characters/54bead23|Osric]] has been here three years and still counts in living ones, which is why he tried. He took it an apple; it ate the apple out of his hand very politely and went back to standing. He took it a rope; it walked with him most of a field, then turned round without any fuss whatever and walked back. He kept that up the better part of a season, in the hour after the forge was banked, which is not an hour a working man has spare.

[[characters/cfe826c1|Jehanne]] watched one evening from the fence and told him to leave the animal be. She would not say why and did not have to; she keeps an appointment of her own at dusk, daily, and has known for years that there is nothing at the other end of it. What she did not tell him was the rest of it — that he had not been trying to move a horse.

[[monsters/white_horse|Snowmane]] has walked people past that gate more than once, at the shoulder of somebody who could not find their way in the dark, and it has never stopped there. It goes with the lost. Whatever else is wrong with the horse at the gate, it knows exactly where it is.
gm_notes: The plainest of the five horses and meant to be the one that hurts. Description adopted verbatim from the monsters agent — it is already the best line available. Osric's attempts rhyme with his own dossier (he walks the meadow every morning waiting for a wife who has not come); Jehanne's withheld sentence is the point of the record and should never be explained. The closing Snowmane observation is what makes the two horses a pair. No stone or leavings bound to it yet — do not invent one.
